fable_followup_summary.object_cues: In the native 210x230 crop the catcher faces the camera in a low crouch. Top-down: tan helmet with brown cage at about x85-125,y0-40 (mask); directly beneath it a large, warm-brown, dome-shaped mass with a clearly curved upper outline at about x94-152,y46-92, which is the mitt pocket presented toward the camera (it is roughly 1.3x the mask width, the expected ratio for a catcher's mitt, and it sits in front of the torso). Flanking that dome on the camera-left side (x80-94,y45-80) is a darker, flatter, less saturated region that reads as the shadowed chest protector/shoulder, visually distinct from the dome by tone and lack of a rounded edge. On the dome's camera-right edge (about x145-164,y66-90) is a small tan oval with a lighter rim and dark center; because it is on the catcher's left (mitt-hand) side I read it as the mitt's thumb/heel edge or lighter welting, though a bare hand cannot be fully excluded at this resolution. Below the dome the white pants/thighs appear, and the two dark vertical lobes inside the drawn white overlay square (square at about x92-152,y77-145) are shadowed thigh/knee-guard regions, not the mitt: they are tall and narrow, not round. Knee caps (white/tan rounded pads) are at about x70-95,y120-150 (camera-left, raised knee) and x145-175,y165-195 (camera-right); the dark-brown shin guards run below those to the cleats at the bottom edge. The batter's gray leg occupies x<65 and never reaches the dome. The white square is a drawn overlay present at the same pixel location in every tile; the mitt dome sits mostly above it, overlapping only its top band.
corrections: Initial claim that the mitt is 'low in crop box area beside catcher's shin guard' is wrong-object reasoning: the mitt is upper-center, directly under the mask (native y~46-92); shin guards are at the crop bottom (y>145) and the dark lobes inside the overlay square are thigh/knee-guard shadow, not mitt.

Initial claim that the batter's leg overlaps the mitt's outer edge in every frame is unsupported: the batter's leg stays at native x<65 and touches only the catcher's camera-left shoulder/umpire region; the mitt dome (x>=94) is unoccluded in all 24 frames.

Initial claim that the crop framing shifts between sheet 00 and sheet 01 is wrong: the static signage letters ('CO rk'), the umpire's blue shirt and the overlay square occupy identical tile positions on both sheets, consistent with the fixed crop [450,240,660,470]; the apparent difference is the batter's stride and nothing else.
Initial frame-127 note that the mitt 'merges with shin guard shadow' is wrong object: the adjacent dark area is the chest protector/torso shadow.
Initial reason text for 114 says the mitt is 'beside' a shin guard; the mitt is above the knee caps and shin guards with white pants between them.
P2 omitted point_xy; it is returned here explicitly as null for every frame rather than assumed.

P3's late-frame posture uncertainty was checked, not inherited: no clear repositioning of mask, dome or tan edge was seen in 132-137, but sub-few-pixel motion is below what the 2x nearest-neighbor sheet can show, so late frames carry lower confidence (noted in reasons).
fable_followup_summary.interval_observation: Static centerfield broadcast view, fixed crop. The ordinal-125 full frame shows the pitcher in leg lift, and the batter progresses from load into stride across 126-137, so the whole interval is mid-delivery. Within the crop the only clear motion is the batter's front leg; the catcher's mask, mitt dome and tan mitt edge hold the same relative layout across all 24 frames. The drawn white overlay square is fixed and sits mostly below the mitt, so it should not be read as the mitt's location.
limitations: 2x nearest-neighbor upscale cannot resolve movements of a few native pixels; 'presented_candidate' means no visible change, not stillness.
Mitt, chest protector and shin guards are all dark brown; the mitt identification rests on the rounded dome outline, its size relative to the mask, and its position in front of the torso.
The small tan oval on the dome's camera-right edge is most likely the mitt's thumb/heel edge but could be a bare hand; the bbox includes it with that caveat.
Bbox is a rough object-reference box, not a measured center or target.
No claims about intended target, distance, or human-label accuracy.

fable_followup_summary.object_cues: In the native 210x230 crop at ordinal 125 the catcher is crouched facing the camera: mask at roughly x100-140,y50-85; dark chest protector with logo directly below it inside the white overlay box; white pants below the protector; left shin guard (image-right) extended toward the lower-right corner with a cream knee pad and dark lower shell; right shin guard (image-left) folded under the body at roughly x65-100,y125-165, showing a cream knee cap on top of a dark shell. The mitt is the dark, rounded, pocket-on shape immediately to the image-right of the chest protector at roughly x138-170,y86-126, overlapping the left edge of the 'co/rk' signage text. Cues: round silhouette larger than a hand, thin tan/gold rim along its outer edge (lacing/piping), continuous with the catcher's left arm coming off the right shoulder of the protector, and it sits at chest-to-knee height in front of the body, where a right-handed catcher's left-hand mitt would be presented. The bare (right) hand is not distinctly visible; it is presumably tucked behind the right thigh/shin on image-left. Nothing mitt-like sits beside the left shin; the dark-with-tan-patch object on image-left is the right shin guard's knee cap.
corrections: Initial reasoning identified the mitt as a 'dark mitt with tan pocket low at the catcher's left shin, right of the batter's back leg.' That object is the catcher's right shin guard/knee cap (image-left, folded under the body), not the mitt. Its cream pad matches the cream knee pad on the image-right (left) shin guard. The actual mitt is on the image-right side beside the chest protector.

Initial claim that 'the crop window shifted downward between rows (116-118 vs 119-121)' is unsupported. The Petco signage text, the white overlay box, and the plate chalk line occupy the same cell-relative position in every cell of all three sheets, consistent with the fixed crop [450,240,660,470] used for every frame. Apparent change in the initial rows came from batter motion, not from a moving crop.

Initial 'partial occlusion of the mitt by the batter's leg kick/stride from 128 onward' is wrong-object. The batter's lifted front leg sweeps across the image-left region (over the right shin guard), never across the mitt on image-right. The mitt is unoccluded in all 25 frames.
